title: Open-immersion direct images
statement:
Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an
open immersion of
finite-type schemes over a field $k$, and let $F$ be a finite
constructible
$\Lambda$-sheaf with the prime-to-characteristic finite
coefficients of this blueprint.
Every higher direct image
$R^qj_*F$ is constructible, and they vanish for all sufficiently
large $q$. For $q>0$ their restrictions to $U$ vanish.

proof.text: Place $F$ in degree zero. Its only nonzero cohomology sheaf is $F$, so $F[0]\in D^b_c(U,\Lambda)$ by [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. The coefficient convention supplies a positive integer $N$ annihilating the finite commutative ring $\Lambda$, invertible in $k$, and $j$ is an open immersion of finite-type $k$-schemes. Thus [cor-fin-deligne-open-finite-coefficients] applies with $A=\Lambda$ and $K=F[0]$. It gives $Rj_*F[0]\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$. Unpacking bounded constructibility gives constructibility of every $R^qj_*F$ and an integer $b$ such that $R^qj_*F=0$ for $q>b$.

source.place: Proof, first sentence (finite-coefficient corollary applied in degree zero)

proof.text: Use the module-sheaf version of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]: for the constant coefficient ring $\Lambda$, choose a bounded-below K-injective complex $I^\bullet$ representing $F[0]$, with injective terms. The statement of that node supplies this representative and computes $Rj_*F[0]\cong Q(j_*I^\bullet)$. This is a resolution in $\operatorname{Mod}(U_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$; no change of coefficient category or passage to derived abelian direct images is made.

source.place: Proof, sentence choosing an injective resolution; module version of the derived-direct-image definition

proof.text: The first assertion of [lem-kun-open-immersion-restriction] says that the abelian-sheaf counit $j^{-1}j_*G\to G$ is a natural isomorphism. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], the module inverse image and direct image have these same underlying abelian functors and the same counit. Hence for every module sheaf $M$ its counit $j^*j_*M\to M$ is an isomorphism of module sheaves: the inverse of an invertible $\Lambda$-linear map is $\Lambda$-linear, since applying the original map to the scalar-linearity equation proves it. Apply this to each $I^r$. Naturality with respect to $d_I^r$ makes these counits an isomorphism of complexes $j^*j_*I^\bullet\cong I^\bullet$. Only the underived counit assertion of the cited node is used, not its derived-global-sections clause.

source.place: Proof, identification j^*j_*I = I; explicit counit argument

proof.text: The module inverse image $j^*$ is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. In the formula $\mathcal H^q(C)=\ker(d_C^q)/\operatorname{im}(d_C^{q-1})$ of [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], exactness preserves the kernel, the image (a kernel of a cokernel), and the quotient. Consequently $j^*\mathcal H^q(j_*I^\bullet)\cong\mathcal H^q(j^*j_*I^\bullet)$. By Step 3 the latter is $\mathcal H^q(I^\bullet)=\mathcal H^q(F[0])$, which is zero for $q>0$. Step 2 identifies the left side with the restriction $j^*R^qj_*F$. This proves the remaining assertion.

source.place: Proof, final sentence; exactness is Stacks Tag 04JC (lemma-flat-pullback-exact, sites-modules.tex) and the kernel/image computation is written out
